name: GDLM 67 physics questions lab
desc: Practice, hitboxes on, record. Do what each label says; read heights on the rulers. Dying or not, both answer it.

lab.name: landing buffer: tap again EARLY (going up)
lab.note: a tap ~0.1 s after the jump, still rising, ~0.35 s before landing: sim keeps a rising press 40 ticks (0.17 s) -> it has run out: DIES at the second spike. Lives = the game keeps rising presses longer

lab.name: landing buffer: tap again AT THE TOP
lab.note: a tap at the peak (vy ~0): sim treats it as falling -> kept until landing: LIVES. Dies = the falling threshold is after the peak

lab.name: landing buffer: tap again on the way DOWN
lab.note: a tap while falling: sim keeps it until landing (seen twice in Clutterfunk) -> LIVES

lab.name: orb: hold the jump into the orb
lab.note: jump and keep HOLDING into the yellow orb: sim: a press held since the ground jump does NOT fire the orb (it was used up by the jump) -> falls in the pit. Lives = the game fires an orb on a held press

lab.name: pink orb launch
lab.note: walk under the pink orb and tap it once: sim launches at 0.72 of a ground jump (apex ~2.1 blocks over the orb). Read the apex on the ruler

lab.name: green orb in the air
lab.note: jump, tap the green orb at the top of the jump: sim flips gravity and throws the cube DOWN first (away from its new floor, the roof), then it falls up to the roof; the gravity portal under the roof brings it back

lab.name: ship heights: floor, roof, slide
lab.note: ship: 1) let go and rest on the floor, 2) hold and ride the roof, 3) let go onto the long block, slide off its end. Read each height on the rulers: sim (lab67.js --check) rests at y 15 on the floor, ~272 held under the band roof, ~118 riding the block (top 90), and is back on the floor (~20) by the last ruler. Back On Track ends ~1 block high after a slide

lab.name: ship corridor
lab.note: ship in a 3-block corridor with spikes top and bottom (Stereo Madness's ship stretch clears only with 14-18 presses a second in the sim): fly it the way you naturally would; the input log shows whether a person needs that many

lab.name: mini step
lab.note: mini cube: jump at the low step (top 56 units, under 2 blocks): sim says the mini cube CANNOT land on it (peaks 4.3 short with the 15-unit snap). Landing on it = the mini jump or snap is bigger in the game

lab.name: UFO: free flight
lab.note: UFO: tap 3 times, slow, read each top on the ruler: sim flaps to 7 units/tick (apex ~2.3 blocks above a flap from rest)

lab.name: robot: free flight
lab.note: robot: one long HOLD from the ground: sim hovers 67 ticks (0.28 s) then falls; jump 0.5x a cube's

lab.name: spider: free flight
lab.note: spider: tap once, then once more: sim teleports to the roof and back (instant)

lab.name: swing: free flight
lab.note: swing: tap 4 times, slowly: sim flips gravity a tick after each press, vy x0.8

lab.name: touch trigger scale
lab.note: walk under both (no jump): sim: the LEFT block (its touch trigger scaled 1.2) rises 2 blocks, the RIGHT one (unscaled, same height) stays. Both rise = GD's touch box is bigger; neither = smaller

lab.name: collision trigger
lab.note: watch the falling block meet the low one: sim: nothing happens (collision blocks not modelled). If the marker rises when they meet, GD's collision trigger SPAWNS its target group (Dash's spike drop uses it)

lab.name: stop trigger
lab.note: watch the rising block: a move (in group 76) lifts it 4 blocks over 3 s; a stop trigger on group 76 fires halfway through: sim: it STOPS about halfway (y ~163, 2 blocks up). Rising all the way = GD's stop acts on something else

lab.name: dual ball band
lab.note: two balls, no tap needed: sim's band for a ball pair is 8 blocks (ball 240; ASSUMED, only the cube's 9.9 is measured): player 2 rolls upside down at y 225 (its top at 240). Read player 2's roof on the ruler
